key_insight: SeasonStereo makes dense stereo matching more robust to seasonal and illumination changes in multi-date satellite images by leveraging generative AI. This expands 3D reconstruction beyond near-simultaneous stereo pairs into realistic diachronic settings.
problem_solved: Traditional stereo matching for satellite 3D reconstruction works best when image pairs are captured at nearly the same time. Multi-date imagery often has major appearance differences from weather, season, and lighting, and large-scale aligned training data with ground-truth geometry is expensive to collect.
method: Introduces a scalable framework for disparity estimation designed specifically for multi-date satellite imagery.
Uses generative AI to improve robustness to appearance shifts between images captured on different dates.
Targets dense stereo matching in diachronic settings where training data is limited and conditions vary strongly.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this enables more practical 3D reconstruction from the satellite archives already available, rather than relying on perfectly matched image pairs. It can improve mapping, environmental monitoring, and change analysis in real-world remote sensing workflows.

paper_title: SeasonStereo: Robust Dense Stereo Matching for Multi-Date Satellite Imagery via Generative AI
paper_authors: Álvaro Díaz-Laureano, Roger Marí, Elías Masquil, Pablo Arias, Gabriele Facciolo
